planting.note: Direct sow in spring or late summer for a fall crop; hill soil around the base as stalks grow to blanch and lengthen the tender white shank.

directions: Kujo Negi is a traditional Kyoto brand vegetable recorded since the Edo period, prized for its exceptionally dark green, tender, glossy leaves and mild, slightly sweet flavor compared to Western scallions. Sow thickly in a nursery row and transplant into trenches, hilling soil up gradually as the plants grow to blanch a long white base similar to a leek, or grow it more thickly spaced for a scallion-style harvest. It tolerates cold well and is traditionally harvested through Kyoto winters, when cold exposure sweetens the leaves for use in nabe hot pots, yakitori, and miso soup. Because it does not form a bulb, cut-and-come-again harvesting of outer leaves from an established clump extends the picking season.

planting.note: Start indoors with bottom heat 8 weeks before last frost and transplant only once nights stay reliably warm; the compact upright plants do well in containers.

directions: Named for its resemblance to a hawk's talon, Takanotsume is a small, slender Japanese chile that sets fruit pointing upward in dense clusters rather than hanging, distinguishing it from similar Japanese types like Santaka. Fruits ripen from green to bright red and carry moderate heat with a clean, fruity flavor, historically dried for storage and ground into shichimi togarashi and other spice blends. Grow it like other hot peppers in full sun with even moisture, and harvest red for maximum heat and the best drying results; whole dried pods keep well for months. Its compact habit and heavy, ornamental fruit set make it a good choice for containers and small gardens.

scientific_name: Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis 'Chun Yeon Gold'

planting.note: Sow in early spring or, better, in mid to late summer for a fall crop, since this slow-bolting Korean type tolerates spring planting better than most napa cabbage but still sizes up best in cool autumn weather.

directions: Chun Yeon Gold is a modern Korean napa cabbage bred for the tight, cylindrical, uniform heads and bright golden-yellow interior leaves that Korean cooks favor for kimchi, wrapped around deep green outer leaves. It is notably slow to bolt, which makes it more forgiving of an early spring sowing than older napa types, and it carries resistance to downy mildew and soft rot that helps it hold up in humid conditions. Keep the soil consistently moist as heads fill out, since drought stress toughens the ribs and encourages tip burn. Harvest when heads feel firm and dense, then use fresh in kimchi, soups, or braises, or store whole heads in a cold, humid space for several weeks.

common_name: Pusa Purple Long Brinjal (Indian Long Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost and transplant into warm soil once nights stay above 55°F; it is grown for both spring and autumn crops in its native India.

directions: Bred and released by the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Pusa Purple Long is a widely grown Indian brinjal variety valued for its glossy, light purple, slender fruit reaching 10 to 12 inches long with smooth, tender skin and few seeds. Plants are early and heavy yielding, well suited to both spring and autumn plantings in warm climates, and the long, uniform fruit is prized for slicing into rounds for frying or grilling as well as for classic Indian preparations like baingan bharta. Give plants rich, well-drained soil, steady moisture, and support if fruit loads get heavy, and harvest while skin is still glossy, since dull skin signals over-mature, seedier fruit. Its long harvest window and reliable production make it a staple variety across Indian home gardens and market farms.

planting.note: Direct sow once soil is warm and settled; this vigorous, widely adapted variety can also be sown again in midsummer for a rainy-season crop in warm climates.

directions: Released by the Indian Agricultural Research Institute as a cross between IC-1542 and Pusa Makhmali, Pusa Sawani is a vigorous, open-pollinated okra with medium-tall, short-jointed plants that adapt to a wide range of warm climates and cropping seasons, and it carries resistance to yellow vein mosaic virus, a damaging disease of the crop. Its dark green, smooth, five-ridged pods reach best eating quality at 4 to 5 inches long, well before they toughen, so frequent picking every couple of days keeps plants productive. The tall, sturdy plants benefit from wide spacing and steady moisture during pod set, and because it is open-pollinated, seed can be saved from year to year if plants are isolated from other okra. It remains one of the most widely grown okra varieties across South Asia for its reliability and wide climatic adaptability.

common_name: Kashi Anmol Chilli (Indian Dwarf Green Chile Pepper)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost; the compact, dwarf plants suit tight spacing and container growing and begin cropping about 55 days after transplanting.

directions: Developed by ICAR's Indian Institute of Vegetable Research through recurrent selection from a Sri Lankan introduction, Kashi Anmol is a determinate, dwarf chile with dark, pigmented nodes and slender green pods held upright in attractive pendant clusters. Its compact stature and short internodes make it productive in a small footprint, and it begins yielding earlier than many taller Indian chile types. Grow it in full sun with rich, well-drained soil, and pick pods green for the mild-to-moderate heat favored in everyday Indian cooking, or allow some to ripen red for drying. Because plants stay short and self-supporting, Kashi Anmol is a good choice for raised beds and container vegetable gardens.
